text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi says, "Our forces are capable of protecting the country's security.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa stresses Egypt's keenness on the continuation of peace efforts. This came during telephone calls with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister David Levy.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri and his Lebanese counterpart Rafik al-Hariri will co-chair the Egyptian-Lebanese committee on Thursday in Beirut. The committee will study the establishment of a free zone and the increase of trade exchange.
- The prosecutor's office decided to try 37 terrorists in a state security court. The defendants planned to rob gold shops and kill policemen.
- Navigation experts welcomed cabinet decisions as the first step towards the liberalisation of maritime transport.
- The agricultur ministry ignores the scandal of British meat entry into Egypt.
